analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Nov 19: Copper Positioning, Supply v Demand, Left hand v Right Hand and the biggest question of all (WEBCAST REPLAY)
key_insights: Yesterday's market move was described as a Covid/Liberation Day-style move on no news. McGeoch disagrees with a colleague's view that the caution reflected limited dollar availability, citing a >$100bn IPO raised yesterday and prime brokerage data showing cash on hand.

US-China framing: the US holds copper and China holds rare earths. The market priced that the US would not tariff copper, which would imply China would not impose a rare earth export ban (Jan 11 deadline). Trump says the US has a rare earth solution, which may mean he keeps the copper tariff option.

Flow data shows a negative arbitrage (large China physical premiums), so the US is expected to stop importing copper as early as December. CESCO says China could re-export more than 100kt in December, with November still looking like about 200kt. The open question is how fast exports run.

The most common client question was whether this is peak US rate hawkishness, and most thought yes. McGeoch says that if it is peak hawkishness, gold is the first place to go. Gold is rarely bought as a single stock and clients usually start with baskets such as the GSXGGLDM index.
Reported Druckenmiller copper selling is read as having sold earlier and probably bought back yesterday. A separate filing showed him buying gold.

BHP free cash flow after dividends and equity investments (including Vicuna/SA copper), FY27/28/29: at $95 iron ore -$2.3bn/$0.9bn/-$0.2bn, at $85 -$3.4bn/$0.2bn/-$0.8bn, at $75 -$4.5bn/-$0.4bn/-$1.5bn. Leverage needs modelling. BHP has sold some infrastructure and streaming interests to fund this period. Copper prices still need to be flexed.

Chile and Codelco: client discussions point to the cost of saving El Teniente and a possible sale of El Abra. The RIO-Codelco JV was also discussed. Options for copper investment include Vicuna, SA copper, Arizona, DRC and Chile, and the open question is how to pay for it.

Positioning: GS thinks its macro franchise was about 5/10 short via options coming into the week. Chinese shorts on SHFE are near local highs, and China added to shorts yesterday. The market has been long or flat copper for two years, so there is room to add.

China had been selling copper to buy gold, and on Monday sold everything. An unverified client report points to A-share short sale restrictions around the APEC summit, which pushed more flow into commodities.

Demand: end demand remains negative while apparent demand is supported by scrap tightness. China has lost about 600kt of metal in scrap, which could reach 1mt by year end, tied to the reverse invoice policy. No sign yet of the tax bureau stepping back or of supply chain changes.

China end-use demand is running -2% to -3% y/y, or about 500kt. Power equipment is the only bright spot. Air conditioner demand went from flat in Q1 to -10% (over 15% of China copper demand). State grid YTD growth is under 5% and its copper consumption is negative y/y.
GS views the weakness as cyclical rather than structural. State grid full-year targets could bring acceleration into year end, and 2027 could be less negative.
Supply: GS sees nothing overly ambitious in its S&D numbers, and a run of company updates is coming (BHP next week, GLEN a couple of weeks later).
Glencore has bought about 58% of its $500m buyback.
BHP Copper SA day is Nov 23 (Phase 1 expansion to about 500ktpa). Phase 1 is in GS base case forecasts and is about one third of BHP's long-run 3-4% Cu Eq production growth target.

BHP Phase 1 capex was last estimated at US$10-11.6bn against GS modelled about US$11bn, with capex peaking near US$3bn a year in the early 2030s. GS thinks mining costs at Olympic Dam and Carrapateena can fall about 40% via block caving and the 2-stage smelter.
GS calculates Phase 1 IRR of about 20% at its long-run copper price of about US$5.2/lb (real), and about 15% at consensus prices.

BHP smelter expansion adds a new primary Flash Smelting Furnace and converts the existing direct blast furnace to a flash converting furnace, plus an acid plant and refinery expansion. Uranium becomes more refractory with depth, so GS expects BHP to autoclave flotation tailings. Phase 2 (a 10-12Mtpa block cave at Oak Dam/Ankata with first production around 2038, and a second Olympic Dam Deeps cave) is not in the GS base case.
Upcoming company updates GS is watching: BHP next week, VALE after Thanksgiving, GLEN in early December, and an expected RIO update.

market_movers.rationale: Copper SA day on Nov 23 covers the Phase 1 expansion to about 500ktpa. GS models Phase 1 IRR at about 20% at its long-run copper price (about 15% at consensus). FCF is negative to roughly flat across FY27-29 at $75-95 iron ore.
Glencore has completed about 58% of its $500m buyback, and a company update is expected in early December.
GS expects an update from RIO that it has not yet seen. RIO has a JV with Codelco.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning is light (market long or flat for two years, macro franchise about 5/10 short), so there is room to add. China end demand is weak (-2% to -3% y/y) but cyclical, and GS is less worried about copper over the medium to long term.

risk_factors: A US copper tariff decision tied to the China rare earth export ban (Jan 11 deadline).
Speed of China copper re-exports as the US stops importing.
Soft China end demand: air conditioners, property-linked consumer demand and State Grid.
Possible tax bureau changes to the reverse invoice policy would ease scrap tightness.
BHP FCF is negative to roughly flat at lower iron ore prices, so leverage and funding of copper growth are open questions.
Codelco and Chile operating and financing problems.
vol_and_positioning: GS thinks its macro franchise had about 5/10 short copper exposure via options coming into the week.
Chinese shorts on SHFE are approaching local highs, and China added to shorts on Shanghai yesterday.
The market has been long or flat copper for two years (similar to gold), so there is room to add.
China sold everything on Monday. CTAs and other systematic positioning were flagged as important in the recent capitulation.
geopolitical: US-China: the US holds copper and China holds rare earths. The rare earth export ban deadline is Jan 11, and the market is pricing no US tariff on copper.
Trump says the US has a rare earth solution. Bloomberg reports he enters China talks facing an AI supply-chain bottleneck.
Chile: Codelco is in trouble, with the cost to save El Teniente and a possible sale of El Abra discussed.
APEC summit: unverified murmurs of A-share short sale restrictions around the summit.
cross_bank_references: J. Currie calling the caution a function of dollar availability, which McGeoch disagrees with.

tension_points.bull_case: The market has been long or flat copper for two years, so there is room to add. Supply growth is not overly ambitious, and 2027 demand could be less negative with possible state grid acceleration into year end.
tension_points.bear_case: China end-use demand is -2% to -3% y/y, air conditioner demand is -10%, and apparent demand is propped up by scrap tightness. China shorts on SHFE are near local highs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs the tax bureau steps back from the reverse invoice policy (easing scrap tightness), or a US copper tariff decision.
